name: Lip repositioning surgery

lead: Lip repositioning surgery is aimed at gummy smiles caused by an upper lip that rises too far. It limits how high the lip lifts, so less gum shows and the smile looks more balanced.

A strip of mucosa is removed from inside the upper lip and the lip is reattached in a lower position, which reduces the depth of the vestibule and may increase lip fullness. A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis measured the short- and long-term reduction in gum display, and the research base is mainly case series and small trials.

paras: It is an elective procedure done by a dental or oral surgeon, with the reduced gum display visible after healing. Technique variations such as adding a myotomy are discussed in the literature. People choose it when lip movement, rather than the gum line, is the cause.
It is a surgical procedure with the usual healing period. Reviews and trials examine relapse, meaning the lip can drift back up over time, and technique choices that affect it.

angle.text: Lip repositioning is used for gummy smiles caused by a hypermobile upper lip. A strip of inner lip mucosa is removed and the lip reattached lower, limiting how far it rises on smiling. The reduced gum display is visible after healing.

lead: Lip repositioning surgery (LRS) is a procedure for excessive gingival display, or gummy smile, in which strips of mucosa are removed from the inside of the upper lip and the lip is reattached in a more coronal position, limiting how far it rises on smiling.[1][2] It is used particularly when a hypermobile upper lip is a cause.[3]

A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis quantified short- and long-term reduction in gum display after LRS and examined the effect of myotomy.[4] Evidence includes case series, small trials and reviews.[2][4][5]
infobox: Elective; a reversible trial has been described

paras: One description states LRS involves precise resection of maxillary mucosal tissue with reattachment of the lip in a more coronal position, which restricts lip elevation and increases lip fullness.[2] A 2023 narrative review covers contemporary treatments for gummy smile caused by altered passive eruption or lip hypermobility.[3] Laser-assisted and modified techniques have been reported.[6][7]

The 2021 meta-analysis of studies using LRS alone assessed reduction in gum display in the short and long term.[4] A systematic review compared lip repositioning with and without myotomy.[5] A 3-year prospective twin study of a modified approach has been published,[8] as has a 6-month study of lip dimensional changes.[9]

Published studies include a case series of seven patients with a reversible trial,[2] a staged case report combining crown lengthening and LRS,[10] a study of smile attractiveness after crown lengthening and LRS,[11] and the meta-analysis and systematic review above.[4][5] Registered trials compare modified techniques, PEEK stents, Z-plasty, Botox pretreatment and healing aids.[12][13][14][15]
